title: Why Betting Apps Give You $1,000 Free (Then Ban You If You Win)
alts: The Betting App Bonus Trap: Why They Limit Winners
How Betting Apps Use 'Free' Money to Hook You
line1: Dave chases a $1,000 betting bonus. 25x playthrough costs more than the bonus. Win? They ban you. Lose? VIP perks. How it really works.
summary: Dave sees an ad: up to $1,000 free from a betting app. Last year Americans lost almost $17 billion to these apps, so why give Dave $1,000? He deposits $500, his whole football budget, for a $100 bonus. The fine print: 25x playthrough required—he must bet $2,500 to unlock it. At standard -110 odds, the expected toll is about $114, more than the bonus itself. To get the full $1,000, he'd need to deposit $5,000 and play through $25,000 (expected cost: ~$1,136). Dave grinds through, gets lucky, and hits +$640. Then his phone buzzes: max bet $2. The app limited him. Meanwhile, Bob, down $3,000, gets a VIP host and free tickets. Data shows ~0.5% of customers generate 70%+ of revenue at major sportsbooks. Massachusetts requires operators to explain limits within 48 hours. A 2026 NYT investigation reported that one operator built an AI model scoring customers by likely losses, directing $400M in bonuses to the highest scorers in 2025 (the operator denies targeting based on losses). The lesson: read the playthrough line before any offer, set deposit limits in app settings, know your right to ask why you were limited, and remember self-exclusion programs and 1-800-GAMBLER exist. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem, call 1-800-GAMBLER (1-800-426-2537) for free, confidential, 24/7 support. Education, not advice.
